newsitem.title: USA: Kmart March same-store sales up 12.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kmart March same-store sales up 12.7 pct.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Thursday that comparable store sales on a consolidated basis in March rose 12.7 percent over the same month last year and U.S. Kmart sales were up 13 percent.

Total consolidated sales in March increased 11.1 percent to $2.92 billion for the five week period ended April 2, 1997 compared with $2.63 billion for the same period last year, the giant retailer said in a statement.
Results exclude sales of the company's discontinued Builders Square operations.

Sales from consolidated operations for the nine weeks ended April 2, 1997 were $4.995 billion, up 7.3 percent from $4.656 billion for the first nine weeks of 1996. On a comparable store basis, consolidated sales rose 8.9 percent for the same period and U.S. Kmart sales rose 9.1 percent.
Kmart said its March fiscal period ended three days earlier than that of most of the retail industry and it benefited from an earlier Easter holiday.
As a result, Kmart expects April comparable sales growth will be slower, said Floyd Hall, Kmart chairman, president, and chief executive, in a statement.
March sales also benefitted from increased advertising and promotion to introduce Martha Stewart Everyday products.

Sales improvement for the month was broad-based, with particular strength in categories affected by more favorable weather and the earlier holiday, Kmart said. Among these were men's and children's apparel, home fashions, toys, do-it-yourself, home decorating, patio, horticulture, sporting goods, housewares, cosmetics and fragrances, consumables, and photography, it said.
Kmart operates 2,133 Kmart retail outlets and has 123 stores in international markets.
